topics.description: A sixteenth-century religious movement that challenged Roman Catholic authority and practices and led to the formation of major Protestant denominations.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man wrote the hymn "A Mighty Fortress is Our God." This man debated Huldrych Zwingli (HULL-drick TSVING-lee) at the Marburg Colloquy and was excommunicated by Leo X at the Diet of Worms (vorms). This man's anger at Johann Tetzel's sale of indulgences prompted him to (*) nail his most famous work into the door of a church in Wittenberg. For 10 points, name this author of the 95 Theses who started the Protestant Reformation.

topics.description: Jovenel Moïse was a Haitian politician and president of Haiti from 2017 until his assassination in July 2021.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader originally won his country’s presidential election in 2015, representing the Tet Kale party, but allegations of fraud resulted in a re-contested election in 2016, which he also won. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this world leader who was assassinated in his home in July 2021 by Colombian mercenaries posing as US Drug Enforcement Administration agents. This leader’s wife Martine was also seriously wounded in the attack.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Moise was president of this Caribbean island nation. A devastating magnitude 7.2 earthquake that struck this country in August 2021 had an epicenter 100 miles from its capital of Port-au-Prince (“port-ow-PRANZ”).
parts.answer: Haiti [or Republic of Haiti or Republique d’Haiti or Repiblik d Ayiti]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During his tenure, Moise faced protests over misuse of loans obtained from this country through the Petrocaribe oil alliance. The U.S. recognizes Juan Guaidó as this country’s legitimate president.
parts.answer: Venezuela [or Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela or República Bolivariana de Venezuela]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2010, this country’s leader, Rene Preval, escaped without injury when the National Palace collapsed ´ in an earthquake that killed over 100,000 people. In July 2021, over two dozen mercenaries carried out the assassination of (*) Jovenel Mo¨ıse, this country’s president. The Duvalier family led this country as despots for much of the 20th century. The island of Hispaniola is shared by the Dominican Republic and, for ten points, what French-speaking Caribbean nation whose capital is Port-au-Prince?
parts.answer: Haiti (accept Republic of Haiti; accept Repiblik d Ayiti; accept Republique d’ ´ Haiti)

topics.description: The al-Anfal campaign was an Iraqi Ba'athist military campaign in 1988 involving the mass killing, chemical attacks, and displacement of Kurdish civilians in Iraq.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler wrote a novel titled Begone, Demons, that features an allusion to the 9/11 attacks. Israel launched Operation Opera to destroy the Osirak nuclear reactor this ruler had bought from France. Apocryphally, this ruler commissioned a copy of the Quran written in his own blood. This ruler was captured while hiding in a “spider hole” during Operation Red Dawn. This ruler’s first cousin was nicknamed (*) “Chemical” Ali for his use of chemical weapons during the al-Anfal campaign against Kurds. This ruler’s forces used the “Highway of Death” to retreat from a 1990 invasion of Kuwait. For 10 points, name this dictator of Iraq who was overthrown after the 2003 US invasion.
parts.answer: Saddam Hussein [or Saddam Hussein Abd al-Majid al-Tikriti; accept Saddam]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A “Hail Mary” formation was used against this leader in battles like 73 Easting. This leader ordered the Dujail Massacre after an attempted assassination in 1982. This leader’s Osirak nuclear reactor was destroyed in Operation Opera; that attack may have encouraged this leader to fire 42 Scud missiles toward Israel during another conflict. One of this leader’s top generals was nicknamed (*) “Chemical Ali,” whose Al-Anfal campaign massacred thousands of Kurds. During Operation Red Dawn, this leader was found in a “spider hole” near the town of Tikrit after being accused of possessing WMDs. For 10 points, name this Ba’athist dictator of Iraq.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Saddam Hussein al-Tikriti [accept either underlined portion]

topics.description: The period from 1701 through 1800, associated with the Enlightenment, imperial expansion, and major political changes in Europe and beyond.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: During this century, Moll King ran an underground coffeehouse in London. A queen in this century sent Gerard van Swieten to deal with a supposed vampire outbreak. A queen in this century inherited Joseph I’s land by the Pragmatic Sanction. Fake Crimean villages were built by Grigory (*) Potemkin in this century to appease an empress who defeated Pugachev’s Rebellion. “Republics of Letters” in this century were supported by Madame Geoffrin’s Salon, which hosted Encyclopedists like Denis Diderot. For 10 points, name this century in which Maria Theresa of Austria and Catherine the Great of Russia were examples of “enlightened despots.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: These people informed Mehmed IV that he was, among other things, the “Fool of all the world and underworld, an idiot before God, [and] grandson of the Serpent.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these semi-nomadic “free men,” who lived in Russia and Ukraine.
parts.answer: Cossacks [accept Zaporozhian Cossacks; or Kazak; or Zaporozhian host]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Cossack rebel Yemelyan Pugachev claimed to be the dead husband of this “great” Empress of Russia, and launched a rebellion. He was unsuccessful.
parts.answer: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II of Russia; or Yekaterina II Velikaya; or Sophie Friederike Auguste, Prinzessin von Anhalt-Zerbst]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Catherine the Great and her actual husband, Peter III, ruled during this century. King George III came to power in England during this century.

topics.description: The 532 CE uprising in Constantinople by rival chariot-racing factions against Justinian I, violently suppressed by imperial forces with thousands of deaths.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: At a competition involving these vehicles, Hypatius was crowned Emperor by a mob of rival fans who came together, chanting “Nika!”; Justinian quickly put down the mob and killed tens of thousands of rioters. The Battle of (*) Kadesh led to the oldest-known peace treaty and is commonly cited as the largest clash of these vehicles in history. The invention of spokes roughly four thousand years ago led to the development of, for ten points, what ancient wheeled vehicles that were pulled by horses?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire's army snuck through an aqueduct to take control of a city from the Gothic king  Vitiges (VID-ig-eez). This empire's historian John Skylitzes (skee-LIT-seez) wrote about a disastrous  defeat it suffered to Alp Arslan in 1071 when it lost to the Seljuks at Manzikert (MAN-zik-urt),  despite the presence of this empire's elite, (*) Viking-dominated Varangian (vaa-RANG-ee-un) Guard.  In this empire's capital, the Nika (NEE-kuh) Riots ended when the general Belisarius (bel-is-AIR-ee-us) slaughtered thousands of chariot racing fans. For 10 points, name this empire that Justinian the Great  ruled from Constantinople.
parts.answer: Byzantine empire [or Eastern Roman Empire; do not accept or prompt on “Roman  Empire”]

topics.description: The 1868–1869 Japanese civil war in which forces supporting imperial rule defeated the Tokugawa shogunate and its allies, leading to the Meiji Restoration.
aliases: War of the Year of the Dragon

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An editorial during this period titled “Leaving Asia” was written in response to the failed Gapsin coup. Forces opposed to the onset of this period were defeated in the Boshin War. Five principles for reform during this period were outlined in the Charter Oath. The (*) Satsuma Rebellion attempted to reverse the effects of this period nine years after its beginning. This period was prompted by the arrival of American “black ships” led by Commodore Matthew Perry. This period began after its eponymous emperor took power from the Tokugawa Shogunate. For 10 points, name this modernizing period of Japanese history.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: According to “The Tale of the Heike,” an archer from this country once shot down a fan from the top of a ship’s mast. In the 1180s, two clans fought the Genpei War in this country. Seven hundred years later, another civil war in this country, the (*) Boshin War, ended with the restoration of imperial power under Emperor Meiji [may-jee]. For ten points, name this East Asian country that, during its rule by shoguns like Tokugawa Ieyasu [toh-koo-gah-wah ee-yay-ah-soo], was home to warrior aristocrats called samurai.

topics.description: A short-lived republic established under Simón Bolívar that united present-day Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This general’s army was once held up by a barking dog, which was then given to this general as a pet. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general, known as “El Libertador” for his role in securing the independence of many South American countries, such as his native Venezuela.

parts.label: B
parts.question: During the Admirable Campaign, Bolívar called for the murder of people from this country. Venezuela revolted against this European power after it was conquered by its northern neighbor, France.
parts.answer: Spain [accept Spanish Empire; or Reino de Espana; or equivalents]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bolívar served as the first president of this short-lived country, which united Venezuela, Ecuador, and its namesake country.
parts.answer: Gran Colombia [or Great Colombia; prompt on Republic of Colombia]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader issued the Decree of War to the Death during his Admirable Campaign. At the Guayaquil Conference, this leader met with his southern ally, José de San Martín. This leader formed the state of Gran Colombia after winning the (*) independence of New Granada. The nickname El Libertador was given to, for 10 points, what revolutionary, who freed much of South America from Spanish rule?

topics.description: A Bronze Age Aegean civilization centered on Crete, associated with Linear A, palace complexes such as Knossos, and sites including Akrotiri.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The eruption of a volcano on the island of Thera contributed to the collapse of this civilization, which used the Linear A writing system. Several bull-leaping frescoes were excavated from this civilization’s palace at (*) Knossos. A mythical Greek king who built the Labyrinth to contain a half-man, half-bull monster names, for 10 points, what Bronze Age civilization centered on the island of Crete?

parts.label: L
parts.question: This civilization’s site of Akrotiri was destroyed in the Thera eruption. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this seafaring civilization, who were opposed by the Mycenaeans to their north.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Minoans were based on this island, where Arthur Evans excavated Knossos.
parts.answer: Crete [or Candia; or Creta; or Kirid; or Kriti; or Krete]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Minoans invented Kamares ware, a type of these objects later Greeks painted in “red-figure” and “black-figure” styles. These objects are made from ceramics.

topics.description: The 1877 revolt of former samurai in the Satsuma domain against the Meiji government, led by Saigō Takamori.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An editorial during this period titled “Leaving Asia” was written in response to the failed Gapsin coup. Forces opposed to the onset of this period were defeated in the Boshin War. Five principles for reform during this period were outlined in the Charter Oath. The (*) Satsuma Rebellion attempted to reverse the effects of this period nine years after its beginning. This period was prompted by the arrival of American “black ships” led by Commodore Matthew Perry. This period began after its eponymous emperor took power from the Tokugawa Shogunate. For 10 points, name this modernizing period of Japanese history.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 1877, these people launched the anti-modernist Satsuma Rebellion. In a legendary story, forty-seven leader-less examples of these people, known as ronin, avenged their dead master before committing suicide. These people’s governing (*) Bushido code draws on elements of Zen Buddhism and Shintoism. Swords like the wakizashi and katana were wielded by members of, for 10 points, what Japanese warrior class of people?

topics.description: A country in southern North America whose geography, history, culture, politics, and international relations are represented across the supplied clues.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the US entrance into World War I, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This document intended to convince its recipient to distract the Americans in a land war so they wouldn’t join World War I. However, this document was intercepted by British Intelligence and used to convince the Americans to enter the war.
parts.answer: Zimmerman telegram (accept Zimmerman Cable; accept Zimmerman note)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Zimmerman telegram was sent by Germany to this country. The note promised this country that they would regain territory that had been lost to the US in, among other things, the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
parts.answer: Mexico (accept United Mexican States; accept Estados Unidos Mexicanos)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This President of the United States during World War I campaigned in 1916 on the slogan “He kept us out of war!”, then asked Congress to approve war following the Zimmerman telegram and a period of unrestricted submarine warfare.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The dying words of this country's last emperor were "Viva [this country], viva la independencia!". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this country whose Habsburg emperor, Maximilian I, was installed by Napoleon III before being overthrown and executed in Querétaro City.
parts.answer: Mexico [or the Second Mexican Empire or el Segundo Imperio Mexicano]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The death of the emperor was depicted in this artist's The Execution of Emperor Maximilian. This man also painted Luncheon on the Grass.
parts.answer: Édouard Manet [do NOT accept or prompt on “Monet”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Both Napoleon III and Édouard Manet were from this country, which was also led by Napoleon Bonaparte.
